rows.design: prospective comparative, two parallel groups; allocation by alternate patients (described by authors as randomized, but alternate allocation is not randomization); assessor blinding not reported
rows.skin_tone: not reported (study site Government Rajaji Hospital, Madurai, India)
rows.patients_enrolled: 15 per group (30 in study, aged 60 to 76)
rows.analysis_unit: lesion (macule); 5 macules per patient, analysed as independent
rows.endpoint_definition: grade G4, greater than 75% improvement in pigmentation, on a five-grade subjective clinical improvement score (G0 none, G1 up to 25%, G2 25-50%, G3 51-75%, G4 greater than 75%)
rows.assessment_method: clinical assessment of each treated macule with serial photographs, graded once every 4 weeks; grader identity and blinding not reported
rows.time_from_last_treatment: not reported: up to 3 monthly sittings 'till complete repigmentation', number of sittings per lesion not given, grading at 4 months from start [about 2 to 4 months if sittings fell at months 0 to 2]
rows.complete_match: not measured (top grade is greater than 75% improvement)
rows.attrition: not reported [Table 1 and Table 3 totals equal enrolment, which suggests none]
rows.citation: Deoson L, Sudha R, Vijaya Anand M. Int J Acad Med Pharm 2025;7(6):765-769
rows.intervention: liquid nitrogen by cotton-tipped applicator (dip-stick), single freeze-thaw cycle of 5 s per Methods (3-5 s in Abstract), monthly, up to 3 sittings
rows.patient_noticeability: patient satisfaction at end of month 4, 4-point scale, counted in patients: score 4 in 10 of 15 (66.7%), 3 in 3 (20%), 2 in 1 (6.7%), 1 in 1 (6.7%); p = 0.035 between groups
rows.texture_or_scar: scarring 0/75; persistent scabbing 4/75 macules (5.3%); no side effects 68/75 (90.7%)
rows.uncertainty: Follow-up counted from start only; final-sitting date per lesion not reported, so months after final treatment cannot be derived. Lesions clustered within patients (5 per patient, 15 patients per arm) but the chi-square p = 0.008 treats 75 macules per arm as independent. Methods say 'allocating them in a randomized manner by selecting alternate patients', which is alternate allocation. Grade bands overlap at 25% (G1 'up to 25%', G2 '25-50%'). Methods say patients reaching complete repigmentation in all macules before 4 months 'would be released from study'; how many, and how they were graded, is not reported. Patient satisfaction (patient_noticeability) counts patients, not macules. Freeze time is 5 s in Methods but 3-5 s in Abstract and Discussion. Results text says 'Among the 15 participants treated with cryotherapy, 5.3% (n = 4)', but 4/75 = 5.3%, so side-effect counts are macules, not participants (Table 2 is headed 'no. of macules'). Discussion says '38.7% had 75% repigmentation' where Results say >75%.
